definitions.explanation: Describing something emotionally or physically difficult to endure. Expresses suffering or hardship.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{辛|つら}いです。
examples.notes: Expressing that work is difficult to endure

examples.japanese: {別|わか}れるのは{辛|つら}かった。
{辛|つら}いことがあったら、{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: If something difficult happens, please talk to me.

examples.japanese: {一人|ひとり}で{辛|つら}い{気持|きも}ちを{抱|かか}えないでください。{誰|だれ}かに{相談|そうだん}することが{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.english: Please don't keep your painful feelings to yourself. It's important to talk to someone.

notes:
辛い conjugates as an i-adjective: 辛くない (negative), 辛くて (te-form), 辛かった (past).

Note: The kanji 辛い can also be read からい (meaning spicy). Context usually makes the meaning clear. 辛い (つらい) expresses emotional/physical hardship, while 辛い (からい) describes spicy taste.
